clue.text: Recoil from a fly in the ointment

definitions.meaning: to recoil is to pull away in alarm or distaste, a two-word phrasal verb
an idiom for a hidden snag or disadvantage spoiling something good

explanation.surface: Someone flinches away from an insect stuck in a jar of cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrasal verb it means shrink back; read as a noun it means a snag or disadvantage.

clue.text: Lives initially wasted in small valleys

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the word for valleys

parts.note: dells are small wooded valleys

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of wasted is used

explanation.surface: Someone's life is squandered in little hollows.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or reside there.

clue.text: Charm a stubborn person with a bit of tenderness

parts.note: a mule is a byword for an obstinate person

indicators.note: just a bit of the word means only its first letter

explanation.surface: Winning over an obstinate person by showing a little kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a lucky trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman worn to ward off harm is a lucky charm.

clue.text: Inform sailor about dance

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to tell is to inform
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Telling a sailor about a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TELL + AB, TELLAB, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is classical theatrical dance performed to music.

clue.text: Food for a home-bird

parts.note: a home-bird is someone who loves staying in, so their food is pictured as a pie shaped like a small country house

explanation.surface: A dish suited to someone who rarely goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: This dish is a British classic of minced meat topped with mashed potato; the clue plays on the cottage in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is a meat-and-mash pie named after a modest rural home, apt for a home-lover.

clue.text: Get in boat at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb aboard a vessel out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to acquire it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: 3 is thrown in prison

indicators.note: thrown means tossed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the clue number refers to the answer of 3 down, the dance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dance is staged in a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Paris fortress-jail stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Olympic Games venue accommodating a mythical racer

indicators.note: accommodating means holding within, so the city name takes the letter inside it

parts.note: Atlanta hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics

explanation.surface: An Olympic host city puts up a legendary sprinter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was a huntress who raced her suitors and lost only to golden apples.

clue.text: Scoring zero-but retaining lead in championship

indicators.note: retaining means keeping hold of, so the word for zero holds a letter inside

parts.note: nothing means zero

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter, here from championship

explanation.surface: A player scores no points yet still keeps top spot in the title race.
explanation.definitionFit: Notching up points means scoring them, from cutting tally marks.

clue.text: Socialist ideal: the end of private property

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from the word private

parts.note: a property is an attribute or characteristic, as is a quality

explanation.surface: A slogan claiming that socialism means abolishing private ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of private property' reads as one political phrase, but it splits: the last letter of 'private' then a synonym for 'property' in the sense of attribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialism aims at a fair, level society in which everyone shares the same rights and standing.

clue.text: Inclined to have a point of view

parts.note: a slant on a story is the angle or point of view from which it is told

explanation.surface: Someone is disposed to hold an opinion of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined in the physical sense means tilted or sloping, off the vertical.

clue.text: A Belgian, losing his accent, becomes a sworn vassal

definitions.meaning: a man from the Belgian city of Liège, with the grave accent dropped from its name
a feudal follower bound by oath to serve his lord

explanation.surface: A Belgian man drops his regional accent and pledges loyalty to a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his accent' looks like speech, but it means the written accent mark on the city name Liège disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a vassal owed allegiance to his liege lord, so such a follower was the lord's man.

clue.text: Most hair dye is manufactured in an Arab capital

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw materials, so the remaining letters are rebuilt
most of the phrase means all of it but its final letter

explanation.surface: A claim that the bulk of hair colouring is produced in a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' drops the final E of 'hair dye', leaving HAIRDY, which 'is manufactured' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Observers captor sets free

indicators.note: setting letters free lets them scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Witnesses watch as a kidnapper releases his hostages.
explanation.definitionFit: People who watch an event are onlookers.

clue.text: Ice from the north-east a politician abandoned here in France

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so these letters drop out of the phrase

parts.note: ici is the French word for here

explanation.surface: A politician abandons a north-eastern region and moves to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes ICI from A POLITICIAN, leaving APOLITAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a layered ice cream in three flavours, originally associated with Naples.

clue.text: Brigands and musicians have it both ways

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
the word it written one way and then the other way round
the word it written one way and then the other way round

explanation.surface: Bandits and a band both want to have it both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' means IT forwards then backwards, IT + TI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old Italian plural for outlaws or robbers.

clue.text: Begin playing hit at university

parts.note: to strike is to hit
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A band starts its set with a hit while at college.
explanation.definitionFit: When a band starts a tune, it launches into it with this phrasal verb.

clue.text: The majesty of King George under a strain

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the royal cipher of King George

indicators.note: to strain is to twist or distort, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: The king suffers under pressure despite his regal splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' seems to place GR beneath something, but it is anagram fodder with A, rearranged by 'strain' to ANDEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty means impressive splendour or magnificence.

clue.text: Replicate a renaissance painting in a church

indicators.note: a renaissance is a rebirth, so the letters before it are born again in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to copy an old masterpiece that hangs in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renaissance' seems to describe the painting's era, but it signals the anagram of REPLICATE A.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture standing behind the communion table in a church is a reredos-style panel of that name.

clue.text: A park official used a bell with hesitation

parts.note: rang means sounded a bell
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A warden rings a bell uncertainly.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden who patrols a national park or forest is a keeper of that name.

clue.text: Loud cries uttered when a mistake is made

definitions.text: uttered when a mistake is made
definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise or apology after a slip

explanation.surface: People shout when they slip up.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means yells of joy; as an interjection it means oops after a blunder.

clue.text: Look round outside bishop's summer house

indicators.note: outside means the other letters go around the letter for bishop

parts.note: to gaze is to look
O is round in shape
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone glances around the outside of a bishop's garden retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden pavilion with a view is a summerhouse.

clue.text: Europeans said to have stoops

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so the word's sound gives a different spelling

parts.note: Danes, people of Denmark, are Europeans

explanation.surface: People from Europe are reported to have a stoop.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop to something is to condescend to do it, lowering oneself.

clue.text: Material for clothes horse taken back on the first of April

indicators.note: taken back means returned the way it came, so the word for the horse runs backwards

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, from April

explanation.surface: A clothes horse is returned at the start of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes horse' is a false pair: 'for clothes' belongs to the definition, and 'horse' is a separate piece giving ARAB, which 'taken back' turns to BARA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine woollen fabric often used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: The elite back off in an ancient city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with its back taken off, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the elite are the best

explanation.surface: The privileged class retreat to an old metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back off' looks like retreat, but it removes the last letter T of BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A great city of ancient Egypt shared its name with a leading city of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Baffle head of 'government with nothing but a flower

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle them

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from government

parts.note: love means nil or nothing in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A government chief is left confused and empty-handed apart from a single bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tall plant with purple bell-shaped blooms, the source of digitalis.

clue.text: Dirty little devil seen by river

parts.note: an imp is a small devil or mischievous child
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite is spotted beside a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclean or contaminated is the opposite of pure.

clue.text: Midwest journalists go to Ohio for coffee

parts.note: the middle of the word west is its central pair of letters
the press is the collective term for journalists
O is an old abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: Reporters from the American heartland head to Ohio for a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midwest' looks like the American region, but it means the middle of 'west', ES.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.
